title: Plan a product launch with the 4Ps of marketing, but only after you have chosen the customer
description: The "What to offer" branch of a product launch.
hook: The 4Ps (product, price, place and promotion) is a simple checklist for marketing and launch questions. Here is how to use it in a case, and when not to.
body:
When it helps

The "What to offer" branch of a product launch.

The checklist

Product

  • Features
  • Range
  • Quality

Price

  • Level
  • Discounts
  • Tiers

Place

  • Channels
  • Coverage

Promotion

  • Advertising
  • Sales force
  • Offers

An example

A drinks company is launching a low-sugar energy drink for students. Product: flavours students like, a can that fits a bag. Price: close to the big brands, perhaps with a multipack deal. Place: campus shops, supermarkets near universities, delivery apps. Promotion: sampling at freshers' fairs and social media. Notice that every answer depends on knowing the customer first.

How it sounds in an interview

Once we know the customer is students, I'd plan the launch around product, price, place and promotion, starting with where they actually buy drinks.

Use it lightly

Treat this as a prompt for your own thinking, not a script. Pick the parts that matter for this client, say why, and leave the rest out. A short, relevant list beats a complete one every time.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. All of these sit on the free frameworks page, next to the 11 core trees.
